chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Hisham and Hammad and Ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr and others, all of them said, he said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no charity nor emancipation except what is intended by it is the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (meaning for His sake alone)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for charity and emancipation to be valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of charity (sadaqah) and emancipation (itq) hinges on the intention being solely for the sake of Allah, excluding worldly motives. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on ikhlas (sincerity) as the spiritual core of financial worship, ensuring that acts like freeing slaves or giving alms are accepted as true devotions rather than social transactions.
